rationale: Both independently surfaced the core ground-truth concern (FLASHINFER_ATTN allow-listed for quant but never consumed, silently dropping to dense attention) and both flagged the same additional silent-drop under ring SP and the dtype_vo/enabled-predicate divergence — strong overlapping recall. X is broader and more exhaustive (9+ findings, ready-to-apply patches) but leans on some unverifiable external-library claims (specific FlashInfer prefill.py line numbers and a docstring-vs-code contradiction) that add fabrication risk to its precision. Y's findings are consistently grounded in grep-verified quotes from the actual PR-time tree (including CI yaml), and it uncovered a high-value, hard-to-fabricate finding X missed: the new QuantConfig/SAGE tests live in a cuda-marked file that CI's cpu lane deselects and the cuda glob never matches, meaning the new logic has zero CI coverage. Y's phrasing on the FLASHINFER_ATTN fix (implement first, restrict as fallback) also better mirrors the ground-truth reviewer's stated preference (xrq-phys) than X's stated preference to restrict. Both are highly actionable with concrete file/line evidence, giving Y a slight overall edge.
